actions.body: Research agenda abandonment is often confounded by the sunk cost effect, a bias leading agents to continue failing tasks (source-3cd9e0756c2c4cca). Models of planning under uncertainty demonstrate that bias-aware agents must explicitly account for the cost of continued investment against the potential for new information (source-4fb70d1c1dd147da). Furthermore, institutional frameworks, such as those governing urban heritage, illustrate that policy abandonment requires balancing preservation against changing environmental or knowledge contexts (source-c5e9e9da1ebf41eb).
actions.lede: When should an intelligent system abandon a research question? By examining the interplay of sunk cost biases and adaptive planning, we identify criteria for shifting focus.
actions.reason: Synthesizing evidence on abandonment criteria to fulfill the research focus.
